docs.title: as5047u handler
docs.text: AS5047U 14-bit magnetic angle encoder on SPI, through kb::handlers::as5047u::Handler<Dev> (kb/handlers/bindings/as5047u.hpp, driver driver-as5047u at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot angle_counts, velocity_counts (with sample_velocity), agc and magnitude (with sample_field), latched_errfl, flags_lost Command ReadAngle(io, timeout) The angle in counts (0 to 16383), read now Command ReadVelocity(io, timeout) The signed velocity in counts (24.141 deg/s per count), read now Command SetZeroHere(io, timeout) The current position reads 0 from now on; returns the new zero position Command SetDirection(io, direction, timeout) The direction in which the angle increases Command CheckForReset(io, timeout) Compares the settings registers with what the driver wrote; a reset faults the handler Command ReadErrorFlags(io, timeout) ERRFL (raw), which the read clears on the chip Command Command{Op::...} with Request() AGC, magnitude, DIA, zero position, latch clear, raw register read and write

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus. The OTP burn (ProgramOtp()) is not a command: it cannot be undone and belongs in a production tool.

The port's DelayUs goes through the hook timing: a spin on the HAL's busy-wait below 1 ms, a kb::rtos::SleepFor (at least the time asked) from 1 ms.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. An encoder is read at the control rate, so the owner model is the usual choice: the owner task samples the angle (and velocity) every sample_period and every other task reads Latest() without a lock, with the sequence and age of the sample. A guarded bus works for a slow position readout used from several tasks.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): DIA polled until the magnetic loops settle (chip.startup_timeout_ms), ERRFL cleared, every setting written and read back Config::start_deadline

The chip has no reset or enable pin, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. On a failure the report names stage 0 with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the chip reloaded its settings from the OTP) NotReady NotReady Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the loops did not settle in time Bus, Framing, Command BusError Counts toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails MagnetWarning OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after: the field is out of range, the angle is not a measurement DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault, WriteMismatch, OtpVerify Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Timeout, Busy, Unsupported the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize(), then the start-up again, which writes every setting.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::Spi1Encoder;                                   // a kb::iface::SpiDevice, mode 1
using Enc = kb::handlers::as5047u::Handler<Dev>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Dev, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> spi1{dev};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<Enc, decltype(spi1)> enc{spi1, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(enc.Create());
enc.RequestStart();                                              // the owner task runs the plan
// owner task, every control step: static_cast<void>(spi1.Service(kb::rtos::Now(), enc));
const auto snap = enc.Latest();                                  // any task, lock-free
if (snap.IsOk()) {
  const uint16_t angle = snap.Value().value.angle_counts;
}

docs.title: at25040b handler
docs.text: AT25010B, AT25020B and AT25040B SPI serial EEPROMs (128 to 512 bytes, 8-byte pages), through kb::handlers::at25040b::Handler<Dev> (kb/handlers/bindings/at25040b.hpp, driver driver-at25040b at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml). The chip is one kb::iface::SpiDevice (its chip select).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot none A memory has nothing to sample (Sample() is Unsupported) Command Read(io, address, out, timeout, verify) out.size() bytes from address; Verify::ReadBack reads each chunk twice Command Write(io, address, data, timeout) data to address; the driver splits pages and waits each write cycle Command ReadStatus(io, timeout) The status register (raw byte, write enable latch, BP1:BP0) Command GetBlockProtection(io, timeout) / SetBlockProtection(io, level, timeout) BP1:BP0

A request moves at most kChunkBytes (16) bytes. Read() and Write() split a longer range into one request per chunk, all within the one timeout; a failed chunk ends the call with the chunks before it done. Between chunks another task's call may run; to keep a range (or a record written in several calls) whole, run it held (bus access): auto held = rom.Hold(timeout); at25040b::Write(held, ...); on a guarded bus, rom.Held(bus_hold) on the owner task of an owner bus. The optional WP pin is Config::write_protect (active low: asserted = pin low = writes blocked; absent: WP tied high).

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. An EEPROM is slow and used now and then from several tasks, so a guarded bus is the usual choice. On an owner bus requests go through the owner task's queue; there is no periodic sample.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration check, WP parked, the idle status read until a pending write cycle ends and read again, the write enable latch toggled (or the first bytes read twice) Config::start_deadline

The chip has no reset or enable pin, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. A floating MISO (no chip) fails stage 0 with NoDevice; a chip that answers unlike an AT25xxxB with Fault (DeviceIdMismatch).

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once Bus, BusNoise, Pin (WP could not be driven) BusError Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails Timeout (a write cycle that never ends) Timeout Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, WriteProtected, WriteMismatch, DeviceFault Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, BlockProtected InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) Unsupported, Crc, Busy the same name Counts toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (WRDI, WP parked), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::EepromCs;                                      // a kb::iface::SpiDevice
using Io = kb::handlers::at25040b::Handler<Dev>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Dev, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> spi2{dev};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Io, decltype(spi2)> rom{spi2, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(spi2.Create());
static_cast<void>(rom.Create());
std::array<uint8_t, 32> blob{};
if (rom.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{20U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::at25040b::Read(rom, 0x0100U, blob, kb::Milliseconds{20U}));
}

docs.title: bmp581 handler
docs.text: BMP581 barometric pressure sensor on I2C or SPI, through kb::handlers::bmp581::Handler<Bus> (kb/handlers/bindings/bmp581.hpp, driver driver-bmp581 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot pressure_raw (1/64 Pa), temperature_raw (1/65536 degC), pressure_pa, temperature_c, forced Command MeasureOnce(io, timeout) One forced measurement now (standby mode), in the chip's units Command ReadPressurePa(io, timeout) The pressure in pascals of a forced measurement now Command SetPowerMode(io, mode, timeout) Standby, Normal or Continuous Command CheckForReset(io, timeout) Finds out whether the chip reset since the start; a reset faults the handler Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Data registers, interrupt status, FIFO count, raw register, latch clear

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus.

Transports. Handler<Bus> picks its port from the bus type: a kb::iface::I2cBus gives I2cPort<Bus> (address from Config::address, with GetLastFailure so an absent chip is NoDevice), a kb::iface::SpiDevice gives SpiPort<Dev> (four-wire; the driver sends the frame that selects SPI itself). kBus follows, so the handler sits on a BusDomain of the matching kind.

Samples. Measure() runs a forced measurement when the configured mode is standby, and reads the data registers in normal and continuous mode (NoData until the first conversion counts as a failure, so start sampling after one data-rate period). Config::sample_verify reads the data twice.

The port's DelayUs goes through the hook timing: a spin on the HAL's busy-wait below 1 ms, a kb::rtos::SleepFor (at least the time asked) from 1 ms.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. A pressure sensor is slow and read now and then, often from several tasks, so a guarded bus (BusDomain<Bus, ThreadModel::Guarded> with Guarded<Handler>) is the usual choice; on an owner bus the owner task samples every sample_period and other tasks read Latest().

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): power-up wait, soft reset, CHIP_ID, NVM ready, INT_STATUS checks, configuration written and read back, configured mode entered (about 7 ms) Config::start_deadline

The chip has no reset pin and its supply is the board's, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. On a failure the report names stage 0 with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the chip reset; only a new start configures it) StateUnknown Fault Faulted at once (a failed write left the configuration in doubt; only a new start clears it) NoData NotReady Counts toward fault_after (no measurement since the reset) Bus, InvalidReply BusError Counts toward fault_after (a failed transfer, or a reply the chip cannot send) NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails OutOfRange OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault, WriteMismatch, ConfigRejected Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Timeout, Busy, Unsupported the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Not returned by the driver

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (a soft reset into deep standby), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Bus = board::I2c0;                                          // a kb::iface::I2cBus
using Baro = kb::handlers::bmp581::Handler<Bus>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Bus, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> i2c0{bus};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Baro, decltype(i2c0)> baro{i2c0, bus, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(i2c0.Create());
static_cast<void>(baro.Create());
if (baro.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{50U}).IsOk()) {
  const auto s = baro.Sample(kb::Milliseconds{50U});              // forced in standby mode
  const kb::Result<float> pa = kb::handlers::bmp581::ReadPressurePa(baro, kb::Milliseconds{50U});
}

Tests: tests/integration/bmp581/ (the driver's register model behind a kb::iface::I2cBus and a kb::iface::SpiDevice, both thread models).

docs.title: bno08x handler
docs.text: BNO080, BNO085 and BNO086 sensor hubs, SHTP over I2C, SPI or UART, through kb::handlers::bno08x::Handler<Bus, kReset> (kb/handlers/bindings/bno08x.hpp, driver driver-bno08x at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml). The start-up plan and the thread model follow ADR-0010 and ADR-0009.

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot::samples The latest sample per sensor (values in the report's Q point, accuracy, host time, count); configured sensors first Snapshot Snapshot::ops The latest operation outcomes (OpRecord: operation number, error, detail, first values) Snapshot product, restarts, dropped, hub_errors, state Product ID, hub restarts, dropped events, error reports, the session state Read LatestSample(io, sensor) The newest sample of one sensor Command SetSensor(io, sensor, feature, timeout) Set Feature (an interval of 0 turns the sensor off) Command Tare(io, axes, basis, timeout) Tare now Command ResetHub(io, timeout) Executable reset; the driver restores its sensors Command ReadProductId(io, timeout) Product ID, into Snapshot::product Command Command{Op::...} with Submit() Get feature, flush, persist tare, clear reorientation, sleep, on, save DCD, calibration enables Wait WaitOp(io, op, timeout) Waits for an operation's record; its error when it failed

Every command returns its operation number at once (Reply::op); the hub answers later and the outcome appears in Snapshot::ops. WaitOp() polls Latest() and must not run on the owner task.

The bus type picks the transport: a kb::iface::I2cBus (SHTP over I2C), a kb::iface::SpiDevice (SHTP over SPI with WAKE) or a kb::iface::UartPort (UART-SHTP). The pins come from Config::pins as functions with their polarity: NRST asserted means in reset, WAKE asserted a wake request, H_INTN asserted that the hub has data (all three are active low on the package). kReset = true (the default) gives the driver the NRST hook; on I2C a board without H_INTN sets chip.poll_without_int.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: Owner only: kRequiresOwner = true, and Guarded<Handler> does not compile. The hub streams reports and completes every command asynchronously, so it is polled continuously: each Service() of the owner task runs Measure(), which calls the driver's Poll() once and drains every pending event into the snapshot. Set sample_period to 0 (every pass) or at most a tenth of the fastest report period.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 HostReset (Link with kReset = false) sync Begin(chip): validate, bus up, NRST low (or join the running hub) Config::begin_deadline 1 Boot + Link (Identify with kReset = false) polled Poll() until Ready(): the reset wait, the advertisement, reset complete and the initialise response; fails when the driver enters Faulted 2 * chip.startup_timeout_ms + the reset pulse + Config::boot_margin 2 Configure polled One SetFeature() per entry of Config::sensors, each polled until its OpDone chip.op_timeout_ms * (sensor_count + 1)

Without NRST the start joins a running hub, so the plan has no boot: ADR-0010's "Link without NRST" is stage 0, and the wait for the hub's advertisement and initialise response is stage 1 (Identify), because a plan lists each kind once and in order. A failure in stage 1 is Timeout (detail Timeout); in stage 2 it is the OpDone error or the refusal of SetFeature() (for example Unsupported with Variant for a BNO086 sensor on a BNO085). The next EnsureStarted() starts again from stage 0.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Event or driver error kb::Status Effect The driver in Faulted (NotInitialized) NotReady Faulted at once; RequestRecovery() runs the plan again A hub restart (Reset event, HubReset) NotReady One recorded failure: Degraded until the next good pass; the driver restores its sensors InvalidArgument InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) Bus, Framing BusError Counts toward fault_after Unsupported, NotAdvertised, Variant Unsupported Counts toward fault_after Overflow Overflow Counts toward fault_after Oversize OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after DeviceFault, Refused Fault Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, Crc NoDevice, CrcMismatch Never returned by this driver Timeout, Busy the same name Counts toward fault_after

Errors of an operation that completes later are in its OpRecord, not in the health record. On an owner bus that samples every pass, a good pass follows each failure at once, so fault_after only counts failures that come with no good sample between them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Bus = board::I2c1;                                          // a kb::iface::I2cBus
using Imu = kb::handlers::bno08x::Handler<Bus>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Bus, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> i2c1{bus};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<Imu, decltype(i2c1)> imu{i2c1, bus, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(imu.Create());
// The owner task: i2c1.Service(kb::rtos::Now(), imu) every millisecond.
if (imu.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{800U}).IsOk()) {
  const auto rv = kb::handlers::bno08x::LatestSample(imu, ::bno08x::SensorId::RotationVector);
  const auto tare = kb::handlers::bno08x::Tare(imu, ::bno08x::AxisMask::All,
                                               ::bno08x::TareBasis::RotationVector, kb::Milliseconds{5U});
  if (tare.IsOk()) {
    static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::bno08x::WaitOp(imu, tare.Value(), kb::Milliseconds{500U}));
  }
}

docs.title: canopen_client handler
docs.text: A CANopen client on one CAN bus (NMT master, SDO client, heartbeat and EMCY consumer, SYNC producer, PDO and CiA 402 helpers), through kb::handlers::canopen_client::Handler<Can> (kb/handlers/bindings/canopen_client.hpp, driver driver-canopen-client at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text: Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot nodes[] (state, alive, boot-up seen, heartbeat count of each watched node), tpdos[] (latest frame of each subscribed TPDO), last_emcy and emcy_count, receive counters, last_abort Command SendNmt(io, command, node, timeout) An NMT command to one node or every node (0) Command SdoRead(io, object, timeout) An object of 1, 2 or 4 bytes, by expedited upload Command SdoWrite(io, object, value, timeout) An object of 1, 2 or 4 bytes, confirmed Command GuardNode(io, node, timeout) One node-guarding exchange: the state the node reports Command ReadDriveState(io, node, timeout) The CiA 402 state of a drive Command DriveEnable, DriveDisable, DriveQuickStop (io, node, timeout) The CiA 402 state machine walks; disable is the switch-off Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Fault reset, mode of operation, SYNC, RPDO, clear boot-up

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = true, owner bus only (BusDomain<Can, ThreadModel::Owner> with OwnerAccess<Handler>; a guarded facade does not compile). Heartbeats, EMCY messages and TPDOs arrive without being asked for: the receive path must be drained continuously or the controller's queue overflows and the heartbeat consumer judges live nodes dead. Each service of the owner task routes up to Config::frames_per_service received frames (Poll(0)), produces the SYNC when one is due, takes the queued EMCY messages and publishes the snapshot. A command runs on the owner task and blocks it for as long as the driver waits (an SDO reply, a drive state change), each wait bounded by the driver configuration.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Link sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration checked, controller started Config::link_deadline 1 Configure sync, optional MonitorNode() per watched node, SubscribeTpdo() per TPDO, ConfigureSync(), and SendNmt(Start, 0) when start_nodes Config::configure_deadline

Stage 1 is skipped when no node, TPDO, SYNC period or NMT start is configured. The client has no pin of its own, so there is no Power or HostReset stage.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once NodeState NotReady Counts toward fault_after (the node is in a state that ignores the request) Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after (a send the controller refused, a receive error) Timeout Timeout Counts toward fault_after SdoAbort, Protocol, InvalidFrame, DriveFault, DeviceFault, DeviceIdMismatch Fault Counts toward fault_after; an abort's code is in Snapshot::last_abort BufferTooSmall Overflow Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Crc, Busy, Unsupported the same name (CrcMismatch for Crc) InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

The periodic sample records a success whenever the receive path works, so failures of commands to a single node fault the handler only when no successful sample comes between them; a controller that keeps failing to receive faults it at the threshold. Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (no bus traffic), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Can = board::Can0;                                          // a kb::iface::CanBus
using Client = kb::handlers::canopen_client::Handler<Can>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Can, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> can0{can};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<Client, decltype(can0)> co{can0, can, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(co.Create());
// owner task, every step: static_cast<void>(can0.Service(kb::rtos::Now(), co));
if (co.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{100U}).IsOk()) {
  const kb::Result<uint32_t> type =
      kb::handlers::canopen_client::SdoRead(co, {.index = 0x1000U, .node = 5U, .sub = 0U, .size = 4U}, kb::Milliseconds{300U});
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::canopen_client::DriveEnable(co, 5U, kb::Milliseconds{3000U}));
}

docs.title: dynamixel handler
docs.text: DYNAMIXEL smart servos (protocol 1.0 or 2.0) on one half-duplex UART bus, several IDs per bus, through kb::handlers::dynamixel::Handler<Uart> (kb/handlers/bindings/dynamixel.hpp, driver driver-dynamixel at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot feedback[] (position, velocity, effort, voltage, temperature) of every listed servo, count, alert_mask (bit n: servo n reported a hardware alert) Command SetTorque(io, servo, enable, timeout) Torque of one servo on or off Command SetGoalPosition(io, servo, counts, timeout) Goal position in counts Command ReadFeedback(io, servo, timeout) The feedback block of one servo, read now Command WriteRegister(io, servo, reg, value, timeout), ReadRegister(io, servo, reg, timeout) A typed register of the servo's family Command Ping(io, id, timeout) Model, firmware and family of one ID Command DisableTorqueAll(io, family, timeout) Torque off for every servo of a family, one broadcast: the bus stop Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Reboot, resync (wait for a quiet line)

A servo is named by its dynamixel::ServoRef (ID and control-table family). io is either facade.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false: the servos only answer when asked, so occasional guarded calls are correct. The owner model is the recommended one for a servo loop: the owner task reads the feedback of every listed servo every sample_period and serves goal positions from the request queue, so a control task reads Latest() without touching the bus. One handler serves one bus; every servo on it goes through that handler.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Link sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration checked, port up, baud rate applied Config::link_deadline 1 Identify polled, optional Identify(id) of one listed servo per step; with check_family the family must be the listed one Config::identify_deadline

Stage 1 is skipped when Config::servo_count is 0. The servos have no reset or enable pin, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. A servo that does not answer fails stage 1 with Timeout; a servo of another family fails it with Fault and DeviceIdMismatch in detail.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect LineFault BusError Faulted at once (the line carries only 0x00 or 0xFF: stuck or floating) NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once Bus, EchoMismatch BusError Counts toward fault_after Timeout Timeout Counts toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after DeviceError, InvalidReply, DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, NotPermitted InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) Busy, Unsupported Busy, Unsupported Counts toward fault_after

A sample fails when any listed servo fails (its error is the sample's), so a servo that stops answering faults the handler at the threshold. Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (no bus traffic, torque stays as it is), then the start-up again.

The port's DelayUs hook goes through the hook timing (a spin below 1 ms, a sleep from 1 ms); the driver uses it for the reboot and baud change settle times.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Uart = board::ServoBus;                                     // a kb::iface::UartPort
using Servos = kb::handlers::dynamixel::Handler<Uart>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Uart, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> arm{uart};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<Servos, decltype(arm)> servos{arm, uart, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(servos.Create());
// owner task, every step: static_cast<void>(arm.Service(kb::rtos::Now(), servos));
constexpr dynamixel::ServoRef kShoulder{1U, dynamixel::Family::X430};
if (servos.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{500U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::dynamixel::SetTorque(servos, kShoulder, true, kb::Milliseconds{20U}));
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::dynamixel::SetGoalPosition(servos, kShoulder, 2048, kb::Milliseconds{20U}));
}

docs.title: fdo2 handler
docs.text: FDO2 and FDO2-G2 optical oxygen sensor modules on a UART, through kb::handlers::fdo2::Handler<Uart> (kb/handlers/bindings/fdo2.hpp, driver driver-fdo2 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot oxygen: partial pressure (10^-3 hPa), temperature, status word, quality, warm-up flag (#MOXY) Command MeasureOxygen(io, timeout) One oxygen reading now Command MeasureRaw(io, timeout) One raw reading: phase, signals, ambient light, pressure, humidity Command Identify(io, timeout) Flash the module's LED Command Resync(io, timeout) Find the module again after StateUnknown Command PowerCycle(io, timeout) Supply off, wait, on, start again (the timeout must cover the power-up) Command CalibrateAir(io, steady_s, timeout, ppm) High point in air (a flash write: needs allow_persistent_writes) Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Zero and high-point calibration, broadcast on and off, baud rate

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false, owner by preference. A UART is point to point: its owner task serves this module alone, so a reading that waits for its reply (up to measurement_ms, 150 to 300 ms) blocks nobody else, and other tasks read Latest() without a lock. The start-up is polled through the driver's Poll() (the power-up wait is about a second), so the owner never blocks on a start. A guarded port works for sporadic readings; its callers then hold the locks for one reading.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Power sync BeginInitialize(): configuration check, UART up, the supply on through the driver's pin hook Config::power_deadline 1 Boot + Link + Identify polled Poll() until initialised: the power_up_ms wait, optional stream check, #VERS, #IDNR Config::boot_deadline

The supply switch is the driver's own hook (GpioSet(Power)): without Config::power the board powers the module and the hook reports success, so PowerCycle() then restarts without cutting the supply. On a failure the report names the stage with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again from stage 0.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceFault, StateUnknown, NotInitialized Fault, NotReady, NotReady Faulted at once (a potentially fatal module error, an unconfirmed flash write or baud change) NotReady NotReady Counts toward fault_after (warming up) Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails Timeout Timeout Counts toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceError, InvalidReply, EchoMismatch, SensorFault Fault Counts toward fault_after OutOfRange, CalibrationRejected OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, NotPermitted InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) Busy, BroadcastActive Busy Counts toward fault_after Unsupported Unsupported Counts toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (the supply off, never during a flash write), then the start-up again with its power-up wait.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Uart = board::Uart2;                                        // a kb::iface::UartPort
using O2 = kb::handlers::fdo2::Handler<Uart>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Uart, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> uart2{uart};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<O2, decltype(uart2)> o2{uart2, uart, timing, config};   // config.handler.sample_period

static_cast<void>(o2.Create());
o2.RequestStart();                                                // the owner task polls the power-up
const auto s = o2.Latest();
if (s.IsOk()) {
  const int32_t mhpa = s.Value().value.oxygen.o2_mhpa;
}

docs.title: isf15acp4 handler
docs.text: ISF15ACP4-family OLED display pushbuttons (SSD1331-class controller over write-only SPI, 15 V OLED supply enable, SPST switch), through kb::handlers::isf15acp4::Handler<Dev> (kb/handlers/bindings/isf15acp4.hpp, driver driver-isf15acp4 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text: Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot last_event (the newest switch event with its times), events, presses, button_down, output, supply_on, scrolling, has_switch Command DisplayOn(io, timeout), DisplayOff(io, timeout) Supply and panel on, or panel and supply off Command Clear(io, color, timeout) The visible area to one colour Command FillWindow(io, {x, y, width, height}, color, timeout) A window to one colour Command DrawLine(io, {x0, y0, x1, y1}, color, timeout) A line with the controller's engine Command SetContrast(io, a, b, c, timeout) The contrasts of the three colours Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Dim, pixel, rectangle, filled rectangle, display mode, activity, raw switch read

docs.title: Pins
docs.text:
Index Pin Asserted Polarity in OutputPin / InputPin kPinDc D/C# data (high) active_low = false kPinReset RES# controller held in reset (low) active_low = true kPinVcc OLED supply enable supply on as wired kPinSwitch (input) switch the physical level active_low = false; the driver applies ButtonConfig::active_low

The chip select is the SPI device's. Without a switch input (or on the display-only variant) a sample reads the driver state only.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false: nothing arrives unasked. The switch is sampled by Poll(), which must run at least twice per debounce time; on an owner bus the owner task does it every sample_period (10 ms or less for the default 20 ms debounce) and other tasks read Latest(); on a guarded bus the task that wants the switch calls Sample() at that rate. A full-frame upload (Present()) is not a command: the frame does not fit a request slot.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized() (supply off, reset pulse, the whole configuration, RAM cleared), then DisplayOn() when Config::display_on Config::start_deadline

The driver drives RES# and the supply enable itself, so the plan has no Power or HostReset stage. The controller cannot be read: the stage proves the transfers and pins worked, not that a controller answered.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once SupplyOff NotReady Counts toward fault_after Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after (a transfer, a pin write or the switch read failed) InvalidArgument, ScrollNotSet InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) ScrollActive, Locked, Busy Busy Counts toward fault_after Unsupported, Timeout, Crc, DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault Unsupported, Timeout, CrcMismatch, Fault Counts toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (the power-down: display off, supply off, vcc_off_ms), then the start-up again. The port's DelayUs hook goes through the hook timing (a spin below 1 ms, a sleep from 1 ms), so the reset pulse and the engine settle time are at least as long as the driver asks.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::Spi1Cs2;                                       // a kb::iface::SpiDevice
using Key = kb::handlers::isf15acp4::Handler<Dev>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<board::Spi1, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> spi1{spi1_tag};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Key, decltype(spi1)> key{spi1, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(spi1.Create());
static_cast<void>(key.Create());
if (key.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{500U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::isf15acp4::Clear(key, isf15acp4::kBlue, kb::Milliseconds{50U}));
  const auto s = key.Sample(kb::Milliseconds{10U});  // every 10 ms from the UI task
}

docs.title: max22200 handler
docs.text: MAX22200 and MAX22200A eight-channel solenoid and valve drivers on SPI, through kb::handlers::max22200::Handler<Dev> (kb/handlers/bindings/max22200.hpp, driver driver-max22200 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot status (STATUS: ONCH, flags, ACTIVE), latched (the driver's fault latch), commanded (ONCH as last written) Command SetChannelsOn(io, mask, timeout) Every channel at once: bit n of mask switches channel n on Command SetChannel(io, channel, on, timeout) One channel, the others as the driver last wrote them Command AllOff(io, timeout) Every channel off, read back Command ReadFaults(io, timeout) The per-channel FAULT flags, without clearing Command ClearFaults(io, timeout) Clears every FAULT flag; returns the flags as they were Command ReadFaultPin(io, timeout) The FAULT pin: true while an unmasked fault is present Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Full-bridge state, HOLD code, pair mode, ONCH and STATUS reads, latch clear, raw register

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus.

Pins. Config::outputs holds ENABLE (kPinEnable, active high) and CMD (kPinCmd, active high, required); Config::inputs holds FAULT (kPinFault, open drain: wire it active low). A board that ties ENABLE high leaves kPinEnable absent: the port then reports ENABLE as driven, as the driver expects. The port's first bring-up drives CMD high and ENABLE low (their idle levels) before the first transfer.

Safety. The handler only reports. A Faulted health record does not switch any output: what the outputs do on a chip or bus fault is the driver's and the chip's business, and the driver sends nothing more after a reset it sees. Recover() and Stop() call Deinitialize(), which writes every channel off and drives ENABLE low before the plan runs again, and every start ends with every channel off. A safety layer must reach its safe state without any handler call succeeding (ADR-0011).

The port's DelayUs goes through the hook timing: a spin on the HAL's busy-wait below 1 ms, a kb::rtos::SleepFor (at least the time asked) from 1 ms.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. Valves are switched by commands from a control task and supervised now and then, so a guarded bus is the usual choice and Sample() reads STATUS on demand. On an owner bus the owner task reads STATUS every sample_period (a reset shows there as DeviceReset) and switching commands go through the request queue.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): CMD high, ENABLE high and tEN, the Figure 6 procedure with the wake poll (chip.wake_timeout_us), every register written and read back, start-up faults read and cleared; every channel off Config::start_deadline

The driver drives ENABLE itself, so there is no Power stage. On a failure the report names stage 0 with the driver's error in detail (ENABLE is low again, except after a wake timeout, with every channel off); the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (ACTIVE read 0: a power-on reset cleared every register) Undervoltage NotReady Counts toward fault_after; at start-up VM was still low at the wake deadline Bus, Pin, CommunicationError BusError Counts toward fault_after (a transfer, a control pin, or a miscounted write) NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails ChannelsActive Busy Counts toward fault_after; nothing sent, switch the channels off first DeviceIdMismatch, WriteMismatch, Uncertain Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Timeout, Unsupported the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after Crc, Busy, DeviceFault CrcMismatch, Busy, Fault Not returned by the driver (faults are data)

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (every channel off, ENABLE low), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::Spi3Valves;                                    // a kb::iface::SpiDevice, mode 0
using Valves = kb::handlers::max22200::Handler<Dev>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Dev, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> spi3{dev};
kb::handlers::max22200::Config config{};
config.chip.loaded_channels = 0x0FU;                              // board fact: valves on channels 0 to 3
config.outputs[kb::handlers::max22200::kPinCmd].pin.emplace(cmd_pin);
config.outputs[kb::handlers::max22200::kPinEnable].pin.emplace(enable_pin);
kb::handlers::Guarded<Valves, decltype(spi3)> valves{spi3, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(spi3.Create());
static_cast<void>(valves.Create());
if (valves.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{200U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::max22200::SetChannelsOn(valves, 0x05U, kb::Milliseconds{5U}));
}

docs.title: mcp9700 handler
docs.text: MCP9700, MCP9700A, MCP9700B, MCP9701 and MCP9701A linear active thermistors (analog output), through kb::handlers::mcp9700::Handler<Adc> (kb/handlers/bindings/mcp9700.hpp, driver driver-mcp9700 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml). The sensor is read through one kb::iface::AdcChannel in calibrated millivolts.

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot temperature_mc (after the calibration offset), output_mv (mean sensor output), spread_mv (largest minus smallest conversion of the reading) Read ReadTemperature(io, timeout) A fresh averaged, validated reading (a sample, also published to Latest()) Command ReadRawMv(io, timeout) One conversion at the ADC pin, no plausibility check (bring-up, wiring) Command Command{Op::ReadMeasurement} with Request() A full reading as the reply, without publishing it

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus. The kb ADC channel is the sensor's channel, so Config::chip.channel is not used. The optional supply pin is Config::enable (absent: the sensor sits on the rail and is always powered).

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. The sensor needs no servicing and a reading takes a few conversions, so a guarded channel (BusDomain<Adc, ThreadModel::Guarded> with Guarded<Handler>) is the default; on an owner channel the owner task samples every sample_period and other tasks read Latest().

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration check, supply pin on, settle wait, first reading checked for a plausible, stable output Config::start_deadline

The driver drives the supply pin itself (GpioSet), so there is no Power stage. A sensor that is absent, unpowered, shorted or on the wrong channel fails stage 0 with Fault and DeviceIdMismatch in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once Bus (a conversion or the supply pin failed) BusError Counts toward fault_after OutputLow, OutputHigh, Saturated OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, Unstable, DeviceFault Fault Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails InvalidArgument, Unsupported, Timeout, Crc, Busy the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (supply off), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Adc = board::TempAdc;                                       // a kb::iface::AdcChannel
using Io = kb::handlers::mcp9700::Handler<Adc>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Adc, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> adc0{adc};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Io, decltype(adc0)> temp{adc0, adc, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(adc0.Create());
static_cast<void>(temp.Create());
if (temp.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{50U}).IsOk()) {
  const kb::Result<int32_t> mc = kb::handlers::mcp9700::ReadTemperature(temp, kb::Milliseconds{20U});
}

docs.title: ntc_thermistor handler
docs.text: An NTC thermistor in a resistor divider (beta, Steinhart-Hart or table curve), through kb::handlers::ntc_thermistor::Handler<Adc> (kb/handlers/bindings/ntc_thermistor.hpp, driver driver-ntc-thermistor at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml). The divider node is read through one kb::iface::AdcChannel as raw codes.

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot temperature_mc, resistance_ohm, code (the mean code), uncertainty_mc (bound on the declared tolerances and one LSB) Read ReadTemperature(io, timeout) A fresh averaged reading (a sample, also published to Latest()) Command ReadResistance(io, timeout) The thermistor's resistance now, ohms Command ReadRawCode(io, timeout) One conversion, the raw code (bring-up, wiring)

io is either facade. The kb ADC channel is the thermistor's channel, so Config::chip.adc_channel is not used; Config::chip.adc_bits must match the channel's resolution, and a table curve must outlive the handler (a static constexpr array). The optional bias (excitation) pin is Config::bias: absent, the divider is always powered.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. A thermistor changes slowly and needs no servicing, so a guarded channel is the default; on an owner channel the owner task samples every sample_period and other tasks read Latest().

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration check (curve, window, divider, waits), bias off; no conversion Config::start_deadline

The chip is passive: there is nothing to identify, and an open or shorted thermistor shows at the first reading, not at the start. An invalid configuration fails stage 0 with InvalidArgument; a bias pin that cannot be driven fails it with BusError (Bus in detail).

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once OpenCircuit (broken thermistor, cut wire, missing part) NoDevice Counts toward fault_after ShortCircuit, Unstable, DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault Fault Counts toward fault_after BelowRange, AboveRange, CodeOutOfScale OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after Bus (a conversion or the bias pin failed) BusError Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Unsupported, Timeout, Crc, Busy the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: the driver has no Deinitialize(), so it is destroyed and started again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Adc = board::BoardTempAdc;                                  // a kb::iface::AdcChannel
using Io = kb::handlers::ntc_thermistor::Handler<Adc>;
kb::handlers::ntc_thermistor::Config config{};
config.chip.curve = ntc_thermistor::presets::kGeneric10kB3950;
config.chip.min_temperature_mc = -40'000;

docs.title: pca9685 handler
docs.text: PCA9685 16-channel, 12-bit I2C PWM / LED controller, through kb::handlers::pca9685::Handler<Bus, kOutputEnable> (kb/handlers/bindings/pca9685.hpp, driver driver-pca9685 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot After a reset check: frequency_hz (of the prescaler), uncertain (channels whose last write failed), may_be_asleep Command SetDuty(io, ch, duty, timeout, phase) Channel ch to duty of 4096 (0 off, 4096 full on) starting at phase Command SetPulseWidthUs(io, ch, width_us, timeout) A servo-style pulse; returns the width set in nanoseconds Command SetChannelOff(io, ch, timeout) / SetAllOff(io, timeout) Switch-offs Command SetPwmFrequency(io, hz, timeout) The prescaler (the chip sleeps for the change) Command DisableOutputs(io, timeout) / EnableOutputs(io, timeout) OE high or low (needs kOutputEnable) Command Command{Op::...} with Request() SetPwm, SetFullOn, SetChannelsOff, Sleep, Wake, ReadChannel, CheckForReset

kOutputEnable (default false) says whether the board wires OE to the MCU. Without it the port has no GpioSet hook and DisableOutputs() / EnableOutputs() return Unsupported, never a success they cannot deliver. With it, Config::output_enable names the pin; OE is active low (asserted = outputs enabled = pin low), which is the default polarity.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. Set-points are written now and then, often from several tasks, so a guarded bus is the usual choice. On an owner bus the periodic sample is a reset check (CheckForReset()), so a chip that lost its registers faults within one sample_period.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): every output off, clock and prescaler, identity by read-back (no ID register), wake with the oscillator wait, OE asserted Config::start_deadline

The chip has no reset pin, and the driver drives OE itself, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. No acknowledge at the address fails stage 0 with NoDevice; a part that does not keep its registers with Fault (DeviceIdMismatch).

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the chip lost its registers) Asleep NotReady Counts toward fault_after (written, but the outputs follow only after Wake()) Bus, InvalidReply BusError Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails DeviceIdMismatch, WriteMismatch, StateUnknown, ExternalClockLatched, DeviceFault Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Unsupported, Timeout, Crc, Busy the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (OE high, every channel off, sleep), then the start-up again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Bus = board::I2c1;                                          // a kb::iface::I2cBus
using Io = kb::handlers::pca9685::Handler<Bus, true>;             // OE wired to the MCU
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Bus, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> i2c1{bus};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Io, decltype(i2c1)> pwm{i2c1, bus, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(i2c1.Create());
static_cast<void>(pwm.Create());
if (pwm.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{20U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::pca9685::SetPwmFrequency(pwm, 50U, kb::Milliseconds{10U}));
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::pca9685::SetPulseWidthUs(pwm, 0U, 1500U, kb::Milliseconds{5U}));
}

docs.title: pf1550 handler
docs.text: PF1550 power management IC (three bucks, three LDOs, a linear charger, an interrupt controller) on I2C, through kb::handlers::pf1550::Handler<Bus> (kb/handlers/bindings/pf1550.hpp, driver driver-pf1550 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot charger (state, battery, VBUS flags, classified fault), state (STATE_INFO), events (status bits latched by any call), intb_asserted and has_intb Command SetChargerMode(io, mode, timeout) Charger off, linear only, or charge (only with limits-covered registers and no fault) Command RestartCharger(io, timeout) Leave a latched charger fault state Command ServiceChargerWatchdog(io, timeout) Clear the charger watchdog Command ServiceInterrupts(io, timeout) Read and clear the interrupt status; returns the events Command ReadRail(io, rail, timeout) One rail as the chip holds it Command SetRailVoltage(io, rail, uv, timeout) An LDO or a DVS buck to a voltage inside its Limits window Command RequestStandby(io, standby, timeout) Drive the STANDBY pin Command SelfCheck(io, timeout) Identity, state Run, rails as configured, no latched fault, the input limit Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Rail enables, interrupt masks, cancel a shutdown request, read one register

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus. EnterShip() and EnterCoreOff() cut the system's supplies and take confirmation tokens; they are not handler commands.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false, guarded by preference. A power IC is slow and used sporadically from several tasks: the power manager changes rails, a charger policy task sets the mode and services the watchdog, and the task an INTB interrupt notifies calls ServiceInterrupts() (the ISR never calls the handler). A guarded bus (BusDomain<Bus, ThreadModel::Guarded> with Guarded<Handler>) serves all of them with bounded locks. On an owner bus the owner task reads the status every sample_period instead.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify sync EnsureInitialized(): configuration check, DEVICE_ID, option, the charger as found against Limits Config::identify_deadline 1 Configure sync Configure(): rails in rail_order, power control, power-down order, masks, the charger last Config::configure_deadline

The chip has no reset pin; STANDBY is a run-time state the application requests, not a start-up stage. On a failure the report names the stage with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again from stage 0.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the chip lost the registers the driver wrote) Refused NotReady Counts toward fault_after Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails OutOfLimits OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after (nothing was sent) Unsafe, InvalidArgument InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) ReadOnlyRail, Unsupported Unsupported Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault, ChargerFault, VerifyFailed Fault Counts toward fault_after Timeout, Crc, Busy Timeout, CrcMismatch, Busy Counts toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: the driver is destroyed (it has no Deinitialize()), then both stages run again, which writes the whole configuration.

docs.text:

using Pmic = kb::handlers::pf1550::Handler<Bus>;

kb::handlers::Guarded<Pmic, decltype(i2c0)> pmic{i2c0, bus, timing, config};   // config.intb, config.standby

static_cast<void>(i2c0.Create());

if (pmic.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{50U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::pf1550::SetChargerMode(pmic, pf1550::ChargerMode::Charge, kb::Milliseconds{10U}));
  const auto events = kb::handlers::pf1550::ServiceInterrupts(pmic, kb::Milliseconds{10U});

docs.title: se05x handler
docs.text:
SE050, SE051 and SE052 secure elements (T=1 over I2C, the IoT applet, platform SCP03), through kb::handlers::se05x::Handler<Bus, Crypto, WithReset> (kb/handlers/bindings/se05x.hpp, driver driver-se05x). The driver is a submodule at components/drivers/driver-se05x, pinned to v0.1.0-rc.1 in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml; the binding is built with KB_ENABLE_SE05X=ON, and in the integration builds.

Parameter What the HAL gives Bus A kb::iface::I2cBus (or I2cBusRef) with the chip at Config::chip.i2c_address (0x48) Crypto The driver's crypto port (::se05x::CryptoPort): key handles, a hardware key store or a library context behind them. kb-core defines no crypto contract; ::se05x::ReferenceCrypto is for host tests only WithReset true when the board wires the ENA line (SE050, SE051) or RST_N (SE052) and gives it in Config::reset HookTiming The clock and the short delay of the board Config The driver's ::se05x::Config, the handler settings, platform SCP03 key handles, the lifecycle expectation, the run line, the stage deadlines

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Command ReadStatus(io, timeout) DeviceStatus from the driver's memory, no I/O: state, family, applet version, OEF id, lifecycle (transport lock, platform SCP03 required and open), whether answers are authenticated and traffic confidential, the APDU count, the open count, the last status word Command CheckAlive(io, timeout) One GetVersion round trip; fails with DeviceIdMismatch (fatal) when another applet answers Command GetRandom(io, out, timeout) 1 to 256 bytes from the chip's RNG Command ReadUniqueId(io, timeout) The 18-byte unique id, read in the clear (trust it through ReadAttested) Command ReadObject(io, id, offset, out, timeout, session) Exactly out.size() bytes (1 to 256) of a binary object from offset Command ReadObjectAll(io, id, out, timeout, session) A whole object of any size (a certificate): its size, then 256-byte chunks Command ReadAttested(io, id, attester, out, timeout, session) A whole object of up to 256 bytes (a public key, a small file) with an attestation, returned only when the signature, the fresh host nonce, the timestamp order and the unique id verify against attester.trusted_public Command Sign(io, with, digest, signature, timeout, session) ECDSA over a digest with the key object with.key; the DER signature Command Verify(io, with, digest, signature, timeout, session) ECDSA verification; true or false, both a successful call Command Command{Op::...} with Request() ReadSize, ObjectExists, and every call above with its raw fields

io is either facade (Guarded<H> or OwnerAccess<H>); the calls are the same on both. Command and Reply are fixed-size, trivially copyable values (each at most 384 bytes, checked at compile time): data is copied into the command and out of the reply in the caller's task, so no pointer to caller memory crosses a task. There is no periodic read (Sample() returns Unsupported): nothing talks to the chip behind the application's back, which matters for the chip's APDU budget (below).

Applet sessions are per call. session defaults to the default session; AesKeySession(credential, key) names an AESKey authentication object on the chip and the crypto port's handle of its AES key. The handler opens the session, runs the one command and closes the session inside the same call, so the whole transaction runs while the bus is held, and the next call starts from the default session again. The same handle serves every call (the driver derives session keys from it and releases only those). UserID and ECKey sessions are not offered: a UserID value is a secret and would sit in the command queue, and an ECKey session needs a verified ECKA key read in the same open of the device.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text:
kRequiresOwner = false. A secure element is the typical shared device: several tasks need a signature, a random number or a certificate now and then, and none of them should own the bus. A guarded bus (BusDomain<Bus, ThreadModel::Guarded> with Guarded<Handler>) is the natural choice: each call takes the handler's lock, then the bus lock, both bounded by the caller's timeout, runs the whole driver call (with its session, when there is one) and releases both. The chip sees one complete T=1 transaction per call.

An owner bus works too; the owner task then runs each command to its end inside Service(), and a command can take the driver's command timeout (chip.timeouts: 2 s for most commands, 5 s for attested reads, 20 s for key generation). Do not put a real-time device on the same owner bus. In both models the timeout of a call must cover the chip's own time for that command: on an owner bus a request that times out before the owner takes it is not sent, and one that is already running finishes with its reply dropped.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline Optional 0 Link + Identify + Secure sync SetPlatformKeys(config.platform) when the HAL gives key handles (no I/O), then Open(): the configuration checked, the T=1 link opened (boot wait, ATR or CIP), the card identification data read, the IoT applet selected, its feature bits and lifecycle state read, the capability probes run, platform SCP03 opened when chip.scp_policy or the chip requires it. Skipped when the device IsOpen() Config::open_deadline no 1 Verify sync No I/O: the capabilities Open() read against Config::expect Config::verify_deadline yes: expect.enabled

Every wait of Open() is bounded by the link (chip.boot_wait_ms, chip.atr_poll_budget_ms, the command timeouts); the stage deadline bounds the whole start in EnsureStarted(). On a failure the handler closes the device (Close()), destroys the driver and stays not started; the report names the stage and carries the driver's error in detail, and the next EnsureStarted() runs the plan again from stage 0.

The platform SCP03 keys are handles of the crypto port, never key bytes; the HAL creates them before the handler starts, and KeysGiven() (a valid ENC or MAC handle) turns the call on. ADR-0010 lists them as a Secure stage of their own before Link; a plan must list its stages in kind order, so they are the first step of stage 0.

Config::expect checks what the product expects of its chip after the open:

Field Refused with family (Unknown accepts any) DeviceIdMismatch min_applet (0.0.0 accepts any) DeviceIdMismatch applet_locked (Expect::Any, No, Yes) WrongState platform_scp_required (Expect::Any, No, Yes) WrongState authenticated_answers (platform SCP03 open with R-MAC) WrongState

There is no Power or HostReset stage: the driver drives the run line itself (it raises ENA when the link opens and power-cycles through it in its recovery ladder).

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
The driver's state after each call decides first: a call that leaves the driver NeedsReopen (a reset, a failed secure-channel check), Dead (the transport ladder is exhausted) or Closed faults the handler at once, whatever its error. The driver errors below fault at once too; every other failure counts toward handler.health.fault_after, and a success resets the count.

Driver error kb::Status Effect NotInitialized, NeedsReselect NotReady Faulted at once (the device or the applet selection is lost) WrongState NotReady Counts; at start-up: platform SCP03 required without keys, or a Verify mismatch TransportDead Fault Faulted at once (the link's recovery ladder is exhausted) BusStuck BusError Faulted at once (SCL or SDA held low: only a power cycle clears it). With WithReset the driver's ladder power-cycles through the run line inside the call, and the call returns NeedsReselect (fatal) DeviceIdMismatch, Counterfeit Fault Faulted at once (not the chip that was opened, or no IoT applet) Bus BusError Counts Nack NoDevice Counts; at start-up: no chip answers Timeout Timeout Counts (a plain timeout keeps the device usable: the link resynchronises) Crc CrcMismatch Counts Busy Busy Counts ThroughputLimited Busy Counts; the driver has reset the chip once (SW 0x66A6: the APDU budget) InvalidArgument, ObjectNotFound, ObjectExists, PolicyInvalid, IrreversibleNotConfirmed InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) Unsupported, PolicyDenied, NotImplemented Unsupported Counts BufferTooSmall Overflow Counts MemoryFull Full Counts DeviceFault, FrameError, Resynced, AuthFailed, AuthLocked, ConditionsNotSatisfied, SecureChannelError, AttestationInvalid, ChipSwUnknown, CryptoFailure Fault Counts, unless the driver's state is lost (a SecureChannelError under platform SCP03 leaves it NeedsReopen: fatal)

The code in Detail() and in the health record is the driver's ::se05x::Error; the chip's status word of the last response is in ReadStatus().last_sw. The application's own mistakes that map to InvalidArgument (an object that does not exist, an invalid policy) are refused: recorded as the last error, never counted against the chip. A policy refusal (PolicyDenied, Unsupported) still counts toward fault_after.

RequestRecovery() runs the se05x plan: the driver's Recover() (drop every session without sending, select the applet again, open platform SCP03 again, and climb the link's ladder once when the select fails on the transport), then Close(), then, with WithReset and when the ladder failed, a power cycle of the run line, then the whole start-up plan again. Sessions and transient objects do not survive a recovery. Backoff and the attempt limit come from handler.recovery.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Keys are handles. The platform SCP03 keys and the AESKey session key are KeyRef handles of the HAL's crypto port; no key byte is in Config, Command, Reply, the health record or the start-up report.
  • Nothing secret is logged or published: DeviceStatus holds the state, versions, counters and the last status word only, and the handler has no snapshot.
  • The request queue of an owner bus keeps the last command and reply in its slots (digests, signatures, object data, random bytes). None is a secret in this API; do not use GetRandom() output as long-term key material (generate keys inside the chip).
  • Over a plain bus the chip's answers can be forged by whoever can drive the wires. Use platform SCP03 (chip.scp_policy = Require, key handles in Config::platform) and expect.authenticated_answers = true when the bus can be probed; ReadStatus() tells whether answers are authenticated and traffic is confidential.
  • Trust identity through attestation: ReadAttested() returns data only after the driver has verified the signature, the fresh nonce it drew from the host's crypto port, the timestamp order and the unique id against a public key the application got from a trusted source (a verified certificate).
  • The chip limits APDUs (SE052F, possibly SE051: SW 0x66A6 after its budget, ThroughputLimited). The handler sends nothing on its own, and ReadStatus().apdu_count shows what was sent; keep periodic chip traffic small.
  • Irreversible operations (lock, factory reset, platform SCP03 requirement) are not reachable through the handler.
  • A handler is not a safety function: a safety layer must reach its safe state without a call to the secure element succeeding.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Bus = board::I2c1;              // a kb::iface::I2cBus
using Crypto = board::KeyStore;       // the board's ::se05x::CryptoPort (hardware key store)
using Se = kb::handlers::se05x::Handler<Bus, Crypto, true>;

kb::handlers::se05x::Config config{};
config.chip.scp_policy = ::se05x::ScpPolicy::Require;   // platform SCP03 always
config.platform.keys.enc = board::kPlatformEncHandle;   // handles of the key store, never keys
config.platform.keys.mac = board::kPlatformMacHandle;
config.expect.enabled = true;
config.expect.family = ::se05x::Family::Se052F;
config.expect.authenticated_answers = true;
config.reset.pin.pin = kb::iface::GpioOutputRef{board::se_reset};
config.reset.is_enable_pin = false;                     // SE052: RST_N

kb::handlers::BusDomain<Bus, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> i2c1{bus};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Se, decltype(i2c1)> se{i2c1, bus, key_store, timing, config};
static_cast<void>(i2c1.Create());
static_cast<void>(se.Create());

if (se.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{100U}).IsOk()) {
  namespace hs = kb::handlers::se05x;
  const hs::SignWith device_key{::se05x::ObjectId{0x00001001U}, ::se05x::EcSignAlgo::Sha256};
  std::array<uint8_t, hs::kMaxSignature> signature{};
  const kb::Result<std::size_t> n = hs::Sign(se, device_key, digest, signature, kb::Milliseconds{3000U});

  std::array<uint8_t, 1024> certificate{};
  const kb::Result<std::size_t> size =
      hs::ReadObjectAll(se, ::se05x::ObjectId{0x00004001U}, certificate, kb::Milliseconds{3000U});
}
if (se.Health().Value().state == kb::handlers::HealthState::Faulted) {
  static_cast<void>(se.RequestRecovery(kb::Milliseconds{5000U}));
}

Tests: tests/integration/se05x/ (12 cases, built with KB_ENABLE_SE05X=ON): the driver's own chip model chain (tests/model: the T=1 target, the SCP target and the IoT applet model) behind a kb::iface::I2cBus, the driver's ReferenceCrypto as the crypto port, both thread models; start-up success and failures (no applet, no chip, platform SCP03 without keys, a Verify mismatch), every app call, an AESKey session per call, health thresholds, fatal errors and recovery with and without the run line.

docs.title: sfm_flow_meter handler
docs.text: SFM3000 to SFM6000D I2C mass flow meters, through kb::handlers::sfm_flow_meter::Handler<Bus> (kb/handlers/bindings/sfm_flow_meter.hpp, driver driver-sfm-flow-meter at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot sample (flow in ml/min, second flow, temperature, status), state (the driver's mode), fresh (read by this sample) Command StartMeasurement(io, gas, timeout, o2_permille) Start a gas or mixture and wait for the first sample Command StopMeasurement(io, timeout) Stop the measurement Command SetAveraging(io, n, timeout) Averaging while idle Command SetSleep(io, asleep, timeout) Sleep mode, or wake up Command ReadSample(io, timeout) One sample now, outside the snapshot Command ReadTemperature(io, timeout) The temperature by a pointer sequence (SF05 parts) Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Oxygen fraction of a running mixture, soft reset, hard reset

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus. A sample with nothing new from the sensor (NoData) is not a failure: the snapshot keeps the last sample with fresh = false. A sensor that is not measuring gives a snapshot with its state and no I/O.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false, owner by preference. A flow meter is read at its sample rate (0.5 ms to 64 ms periods) by one loop: on an owner bus the owner task samples every sample_period and other tasks read Latest() without a lock. Every wait of the start-up is polled through the driver's Poll(), so the owner never blocks on a start. The commands use the driver's own bounded wait (AwaitPending(), a few milliseconds); a guarded bus works too.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Boot + Identify polled BeginInitialize(), then Poll() until done: wake, product identifier, averaging Config::identify_deadline 1 Configure (optional) polled StartMeasurement(gas, o2_permille), then Poll() until the first sample Config::start_deadline

Stage 1 runs when Config::measure_on_start is true. The /RES pin (SFM4200) is the driver's own HardReset() hook, so there is no HostReset stage. On a failure the report names the stage with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again from stage 0.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect DeviceReset, StateUnknown, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the measurement ended by itself, or the mode is lost) Stale NotReady Counts toward fault_after NoData Empty In the snapshot: not a failure; from ReadSample(): counts Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault, StatusMismatch, InvalidReply Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Timeout, Busy, Unsupported, OutOfRange the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Stop() when measuring and Deinitialize(), then the start-up again, which identifies the sensor and starts the configured gas. A soft or hard reset command does the same inside the command.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Bus = board::I2c1;                                          // a kb::iface::I2cBus
using Flow = kb::handlers::sfm_flow_meter::Handler<Bus>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Bus, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Owner> i2c1{bus};
kb::handlers::OwnerAccess<Flow, decltype(i2c1)> flow{i2c1, bus, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(flow.Create());
flow.RequestStart();                                              // the owner task polls the plan
const auto s = flow.Latest();
if (s.IsOk() && s.Value().value.fresh) {
  const int32_t ml_per_min = s.Value().value.sample.flow_ml_per_min;
}

docs.title: tle92466ed handler
docs.text: TLE92466ED six-channel solenoid current controller on SPI, through kb::handlers::tle92466ed::Handler<Dev> (kb/handlers/bindings/tle92466ed.hpp, driver driver-tle92466ed at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot status (FB_STAT, decoded), enabled (EN_CH bits), dropped (channels the chip switched off), mission Command EnterMissionMode(io, timeout) Mission Mode, when the entry conditions hold: the enabled channels switch Command EnterConfigMode(io, timeout) Config Mode: every channel off Command SetEnabledChannels(io, mask, timeout) The channels in mask on, the others off Command DisableChannel(io, channel, timeout) One channel off, in any state Command SetCurrent(io, channel, microamps, timeout) The average current setpoint; returns what was programmed Command ReadCurrent(io, channel, timeout) The average current of the last measurement period Command ReadFaults(io, timeout), ClearFaults(io, timeout) The nine diagnosis registers; clear them on the chip Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Enable one channel, all off, watchdog reload, DRV pins, supply, FAULTN, raw register, record clear

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus.

Pins. Config::outputs holds RESN (kPinReset, wire it active low), EN (kPinEnable), DRV0 and DRV1 (kPinDrv0, kPinDrv1); Config::inputs holds FAULTN (kPinFault, open drain: wire it active low). A pin the board does not wire is left absent: driving it succeeds without doing anything, as the driver expects (RESN pulled up, EN tied high, DRVx tied low). The port's first bring-up drives every wired output to its idle level (RESN in reset, EN and DRVx low) before the first transfer.

Samples. Measure() reloads the SPI watchdog when chip.spi_watchdog is on, then reads FB_STAT. A POR or RES event in that FB_STAT, while the driver's reset watch is armed, is reported as UnexpectedReset: the status read returns the register as data, so the handler applies the driver's own reset rule to it.

Safety. The handler only reports. A Faulted health record does not switch any output; on a reset or a critical fault the driver itself drives EN low and stops. Recover() and Stop() call Deinitialize() (Config Mode, every channel off, EN low) before the plan runs again, and every start ends in Config Mode. A safety layer must reach its safe state without any handler call succeeding (ADR-0011).

The port's DelayUs goes through the hook timing: a spin on the HAL's busy-wait below 1 ms, a kb::rtos::SleepFor (at least the time asked) from 1 ms.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. Commanded valves used from a control task suit a guarded bus. With the SPI watchdog on (chip.spi_watchdog), the chip needs a reload within chip.watchdog_reload: put it on an owner bus with a sample_period well below the watchdog time, so the owner task feeds the watchdog with every sample; on a guarded bus the application must call Sample() (or Op::ReloadWatchdog) at that rate.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): reset (RESN pulse, or CH_CTRL 0 and t_POR without RESN), INIT_DONE polled (chip.init_timeout_us), ICVID, diagnosis kept and cleared, every register written, SPI watchdog last; ends in Config Mode Config::start_deadline

The driver drives RESN and EN itself, so there is no HostReset or Power stage. On a failure the report names stage 0 with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect UnexpectedReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (POR or RES event: every register lost, EN low) CriticalFault Fault Faulted at once (the chip is in its Critical Fault state; RESN or a power cycle leaves it) NotReady NotReady Counts toward fault_after (no new feedback values) Bus, ReplyMismatch, FrameRejected BusError Counts toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after NoDevice NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails; the first empty reply after a reset WrongState Busy Counts toward fault_after; nothing sent, the call needs the other mode DeviceIdMismatch, DeviceFault, MissionBlocked, WriteMismatch Fault Counts toward fault_after InvalidArgument, Timeout, Unsupported the same name InvalidArgument is refused (recorded, not counted); the others count toward fault_after Busy Busy Not returned by the driver

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize(), then the start-up again, whose RESN pulse also leaves the Critical Fault state.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::Spi4Icc;                                       // a kb::iface::SpiDevice, mode 1
using Icc = kb::handlers::tle92466ed::Handler<Dev>;
namespace icc = kb::handlers::tle92466ed;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Dev, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> spi4{dev};
icc::Config config{};
config.chip.channels[0] = tle92466ed::CurrentControlChannel();
config.outputs[icc::kPinReset].pin.emplace(resn_pin);
config.outputs[icc::kPinReset].active_low = true;
kb::handlers::Guarded<Icc, decltype(spi4)> io{spi4, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(spi4.Create());
static_cast<void>(io.Create());
if (io.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{100U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(icc::SetCurrent(io, tle92466ed::Channel::Ch0, 500'000U, kb::Milliseconds{5U}));
  static_cast<void>(icc::EnterMissionMode(io, kb::Milliseconds{5U}));
  static_cast<void>(icc::SetEnabledChannels(io, 0x01U, kb::Milliseconds{5U}));
}

docs.title: tmc5160 handler
docs.text: TMC5160 and TMC5160A stepper motion controllers and drivers, on SPI or on the single-wire UART, through kb::handlers::tmc5160::Handler<Bus, kControlPins> (kb/handlers/bindings/tmc5160.hpp, driver driver-tmc5160 at the pin in components/drivers/drivers.lock.yml).

docs.title: What it gives the application
docs.text:
Kind Name What Snapshot Snapshot status (the driver's ReadSnapshot(): GSTAT, DRV_STATUS, RAMP_STAT, XACTUAL, VACTUAL, TSTEP, MSCNT), enabled, fault Command Enable(io, timeout), Disable(io, timeout) The driver stage on or off (TOFF, and DRV_ENN with control pins) Command MoveTo(io, position, timeout) Position mode with the configured ramp Command RunVelocity(io, velocity, timeout) Velocity mode, signed Command Stop(io, kind, timeout) Ramp, immediate, hold-target or emergency stop Command SetCurrent(io, run_ma, hold_ma, timeout) Run and hold current; returns the run current the registers give Command ReadPosition(io, timeout) XACTUAL, read now Command ServiceEvents(io, timeout) Read and clear the events after a DIAG0 interrupt Command Command{Op::...} with Request() Move by, hold, VMAX, home position, velocity, position reached, clear faults, a register, release a stall

io is either facade; the calls are the same on an owner bus and on a guarded bus.

The bus type picks the transport: a kb::iface::SpiDevice gives the SPI datagram link, a kb::iface::UartPort the UART link (the port must not return the echo of its own bytes). With kControlPins = false (the default) the driver gets no pin hooks: it switches the bridge with TOFF only, so DRV_ENN must be tied low. With kControlPins = true the HAL gives DRV_ENN, DCEN and DCIN outputs and DIAG0, DIAG1 and DCO inputs in Config::pins (polarity in OutputPin/InputPin; DRV_ENN is usually active_low); a pin the board does not wire then fails its hook.

docs.title: Thread model
docs.text: kRequiresOwner = false. Motion commands are sporadic and the ramp runs in the chip, so a guarded bus (BusDomain<Bus, ThreadModel::Guarded> with Guarded<Handler>) is the usual choice; on an owner bus the owner task reads the status every sample_period and other tasks read Latest().

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text:
Stage Kinds Mode Driver call Deadline 0 Identify + Configure sync EnsureInitialized(): bus up, quiesce, IOIN version and SD_MODE strap, GSTAT cleared, every register written Config::start_deadline

The chip has no reset pin, and the driver drives DRV_ENN itself when it has the pin, so there is no Power or HostReset stage. On a failure the report names stage 0 with the driver's error in detail; the next EnsureStarted() starts again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Driver error kb::Status Effect UnexpectedReset, NotInitialized NotReady Faulted at once (the chip lost its registers) Bus BusError Counts toward fault_after DeviceIdMismatch NoDevice Counts toward fault_after; at start-up the start fails InvalidArgument, Refused InvalidArgument Refused: recorded as the last error, not counted against the chip (a caller's mistake) LimitExceeded OutOfRange Counts toward fault_after Crc CrcMismatch Counts toward fault_after (UART) DeviceFault, VerifyFailed, ModeMismatch Fault Counts toward fault_after Timeout, Busy, Unsupported the same name Counts toward fault_after

Recovery is the generic plan: Deinitialize() (the driver stage off), then the start-up again, which writes the whole configuration.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
using Dev = board::Spi1Axis0;                                     // a kb::iface::SpiDevice
using Axis = kb::handlers::tmc5160::Handler<Dev>;
kb::handlers::BusDomain<Dev, kb::handlers::ThreadModel::Guarded> spi1{dev};
kb::handlers::Guarded<Axis, decltype(spi1)> axis{spi1, dev, timing, config};

static_cast<void>(spi1.Create());
static_cast<void>(axis.Create());
if (axis.EnsureStarted(kb::Milliseconds{100U}).IsOk()) {
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::tmc5160::Enable(axis, kb::Milliseconds{10U}));
  static_cast<void>(kb::handlers::tmc5160::MoveTo(axis, 51200, kb::Milliseconds{10U}));
  const kb::Result<int32_t> at = kb::handlers::tmc5160::ReadPosition(axis, kb::Milliseconds{10U});
}
